+//! The viewport's render pipelines, built for one sample count (#2958):
+//! every pipeline of the 3D pass must match the pass's targets, so a new
+//! anti-aliasing choice rebuilds this whole set (and the traced-stock
+//! composite, `trace::composite`) and nothing else.
+//! Provenance: our own code, moved out of `viewport.rs` (the descriptors
+//! are unchanged apart from the sample count and the wide overlay lines);
+//! specced from the wgpu documentation.
+
+use egui_wgpu::wgpu;
+
+use super::wide::SEGMENT_LAYOUT;
+use super::{DEPTH_FORMAT, VERTEX_LAYOUT};
+
+pub(super) struct Pipes {
+    pub pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    /// Faces that only write depth - the wireframe mode's hidden-line
+    /// prepass (same vertex stage and culling as `pipeline`, no color).
+    pub depth_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    pub line_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    /// The model wire behind the faces ("Shaded, with hidden edges", #2818).
+    pub hidden_line_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    pub stock_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    pub region_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+    /// #2958: the overlay as wide anti-aliased quads, one instance per
+    /// segment (`viewport::wide`).
+    pub wide_pipeline: wgpu::RenderPipeline,
+}
+
+/// Translucent over what is there; the target's alpha stays as it is (the
+/// egui texture keeps an opaque viewport).
+const OVER: wgpu::BlendState = wgpu::BlendState {
+    color: wgpu::BlendComponent {
+        src_factor: wgpu::BlendFactor::SrcAlpha,
+        dst_factor: wgpu::BlendFactor::OneMinusSrcAlpha,
+        operation: wgpu::BlendOperation::Add,
+    },
+    alpha: wgpu::BlendComponent {
+        src_factor: wgpu::BlendFactor::Zero,
+        dst_factor: wgpu::BlendFactor::One,
+        operation: wgpu::BlendOperation::Add,
+    },
+};
+
+/// What differs between the viewport's pipelines.
+struct Spec {
+    label: &'static str,
+    vs: &'static str,
+    fs: &'static str,
+    buffer: wgpu::VertexBufferLayout<'static>,
+    topology: wgpu::PrimitiveTopology,
+    cull: Option<wgpu::Face>,
+    depth_write: bool,
+    compare: wgpu::CompareFunction,
+    blend: Option<wgpu::BlendState>,
+    writes: wgpu::ColorWrites,
+}
+
+pub(super) fn build(
+    device: &wgpu::Device,
+    shader: &wgpu::ShaderModule,
+    layout: &wgpu::PipelineLayout,
+    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
+    samples: u32,
+) -> Pipes {
+    let make = |s: Spec| {
+        device.create_render_pipeline(&wgpu::RenderPipelineDescriptor {
+            label: Some(s.label),
+            layout: Some(layout),
+            vertex: wgpu::VertexState {
+                module: shader,
+                entry_point: Some(s.vs),
+                compilation_options: Default::default(),
+                buffers: &[Some(s.buffer)],
+            },
+            primitive: wgpu::PrimitiveState {
+                topology: s.topology,
+                front_face: wgpu::FrontFace::Ccw,
+                cull_mode: s.cull,
+                ..Default::default()
+            },
+            depth_stencil: Some(wgpu::DepthStencilState {
+                format: DEPTH_FORMAT,
+                depth_write_enabled: Some(s.depth_write),
+                depth_compare: Some(s.compare),
+                stencil: wgpu::StencilState::default(),
+                bias: wgpu::DepthBiasState::default(),
+            }),
+            multisample: wgpu::MultisampleState { count: samples, ..Default::default() },
+            fragment: Some(wgpu::FragmentState {
+                module: shader,
+                entry_point: Some(s.fs),
+                compilation_options: Default::default(),
+                targets: &[Some(wgpu::ColorTargetState { format, blend: s.blend, write_mask: s.writes })],
+            }),
+            multiview_mask: None,
+            cache: None,
+        })
+    };
+    let tri = wgpu::PrimitiveTopology::TriangleList;
+    let back = Some(wgpu::Face::Back);
+    let (less, less_eq) = (wgpu::CompareFunction::Less, wgpu::CompareFunction::LessEqual);
+    let all = wgpu::ColorWrites::ALL;
+    let solid = |label, fs, depth_write, blend, writes| Spec {
+        label,
+        vs: "vs_main",
+        fs,
+        buffer: VERTEX_LAYOUT,
+        topology: tri,
+        cull: back,
+        depth_write,
+        compare: less,
+        blend,
+        writes,
+    };
+    Pipes {
+        pipeline: make(solid("viewport3d-pipe", "fs_main", true, None, all)),
+        // Depth-only pass for wireframe mode: the same solid geometry,
+        // rasterized with color writes off. Faces occlude the far wire
+        // exactly as they occlude it when lit - the hidden-line law is
+        // then one branch in `render`, not a second geometry.
+        depth_pipeline: make(solid("viewport3d-depth", "fs_edge", true, None, wgpu::ColorWrites::empty())),
+        // Facet edges over the shaded pass. No culling (back-face wire is
+        // hidden by depth anyway). Lines may not carry a depth bias in
+        // wgpu, so edges win ties against the faces they lie on via
+        // LessEqual instead.
+        line_pipeline: make(Spec {
+            label: "viewport3d-lines",
+            topology: wgpu::PrimitiveTopology::LineList,
+            cull: None,
+            depth_write: false,
+            compare: less_eq,
+            ..solid("", "fs_edge", false, None, all)
+        }),
+        // The hidden-edge pipeline (#2818) is the same wire with the depth
+        // test reversed: it draws only where a face is in front, blended.
+        hidden_line_pipeline: make(Spec {
+            label: "viewport3d-hidden-lines",
+            topology: wgpu::PrimitiveTopology::LineList,
+            cull: None,
+            depth_write: false,
+            compare: wgpu::CompareFunction::Greater,
+            ..solid("", "fs_edge_hidden", false, Some(wgpu::BlendState::ALPHA_BLENDING), all)
+        }),
+        // Translucent stock: blended over whatever the opaque pass left,
+        // never writing depth (models stay pickable-and-visible through it).
+        stock_pipeline: make(solid("viewport3d-stock", "fs_stock", false, Some(OVER), all)),
+        // Cut-region fill: the stock blend's shape (last, translucent, no
+        // depth write) with a constant color.
+        region_pipeline: make(solid("viewport3d-region", "fs_region", false, Some(OVER), all)),
+        // The overlay (toolpaths, height planes, outlines, triads, grid):
+        // depth-tested, never writing depth, blended by its coverage.
+        wide_pipeline: make(Spec {
+            label: "viewport3d-wide",
+            vs: "vs_wide",
+            fs: "fs_wide",
+            buffer: SEGMENT_LAYOUT,
+            topology: tri,
+            cull: None,
+            depth_write: false,
+            compare: less_eq,
+            blend: Some(OVER),
+            writes: all,
+        }),
+    }
+}
+
+/// The pass's targets for one sample count.
+pub(super) struct Targets {
+    /// The multisample colour target (`None` at 1 sample per pixel).
+    pub msaa: Option<wgpu::Texture>,
+    pub msaa_view: Option<wgpu::TextureView>,
+    /// The single-sample colour the shell shows and tests read back.
+    pub color: wgpu::Texture,
+    pub color_view: wgpu::TextureView,
+    pub depth: wgpu::Texture,
+    pub depth_view: wgpu::TextureView,
+}
+
+fn extent(width: u32, height: u32) -> wgpu::Extent3d {
+    wgpu::Extent3d { width: width.max(1), height: height.max(1), depth_or_array_layers: 1 }
+}
+
+pub(super) fn make_targets(
+    device: &wgpu::Device,
+    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
+    width: u32,
+    height: u32,
+    samples: u32,
+) -> Targets {
+    let color = device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
+        label: Some("viewport3d-color"),
+        size: extent(width, height),
+        mip_level_count: 1,
+        sample_count: 1,
+        dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
+        format,
+        // COPY_SRC lets tests read the frame back (View3D::snapshot_rgba);
+        // for the app the flag costs nothing at runtime.
+        usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT
+            | wgpu::TextureUsages::TEXTURE_BINDING
+            | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_SRC,
+        view_formats: &[],
+    });
+    let color_view = color.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default());
+    let (msaa, depth) = make_sample_targets(device, format, width, height, samples);
+    let msaa_view = msaa.as_ref().map(|t| t.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default()));
+    let depth_view = depth.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default());
+    Targets { msaa, msaa_view, color, color_view, depth, depth_view }
+}
+
+/// The targets whose sample count follows the anti-aliasing: the
+/// multisample colour (none at 1) and the depth.
+pub(super) fn make_sample_targets(
+    device: &wgpu::Device,
+    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
+    width: u32,
+    height: u32,
+    samples: u32,
+) -> (Option<wgpu::Texture>, wgpu::Texture) {
+    let target = |label, format, usage| {
+        device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
+            label: Some(label),
+            size: extent(width, height),
+            mip_level_count: 1,
+            sample_count: samples,
+            dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
+            format,
+            usage,
+            view_formats: &[],
+        })
+    };
+    let msaa = (samples > 1).then(|| target("viewport3d-msaa", format, wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT));
+    let depth = target("viewport3d-depth", DEPTH_FORMAT, wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT);
+    (msaa, depth)
+}

+## #2958 - Viewport overlay as wide anti-aliased lines, with MSAA
+
+**What was decided.**
+
+- The viewport overlay draws as screen-facing quads, one 32-byte instance for each segment (two f32x3 points and two RGBA8 colours). The vertex shader makes the six corners. The fragment shader fades the sides and the ends over one pixel. The old 1 px `LineList` overlay pipeline is removed.
+- The overlay includes toolpaths, height planes, region outlines, triads, the ground grid and the other overlay lines. All of these use the one width.
+- The default width is 1.5 pt, multiplied by the display's pixels per point. The choices are 1, 1.5, 2 and 3 pt.
+- Each wide-line vertex moves toward the eye by `LIFT_WIDTHS` = 3 line widths of world distance. The world size of one pixel comes from the `mvp` matrix, so the lift is correct in perspective and in orthographic projection.
+- Each end of a line extends half the line width past its point. Two lines that meet thus close the corner and do not overlap past it.
+- MSAA is a setting: Off, 2x or 4x. The default is 4x. All the viewport pipelines and the traced-stock composite use the same sample count. A change rebuilds the pipelines and the multisample and depth targets. The resolved colour target stays, so the egui texture stays bound.
+- The windowed shell requests `TEXTURE_ADAPTER_SPECIFIC_FORMAT_FEATURES` when the adapter has it, and reads the adapter's sample counts for the colour and depth formats. Without the feature, only WebGPU's guaranteed counts (1 and 4) are offered. The browser build always offers only 1 and 4.
+- An anti-aliasing row for a count that the device does not offer is disabled, and its hover text gives the reason. A queued pick of such a count is refused by name.
+- A kept count that the device does not offer falls back to the highest offered count below it. The status line says so once.
+- The two settings are per-user view settings in `view.json` (`app::view`), with the origin-name switch. They are not in `prefs.json`. They are not on the undo history and do not make the document unsaved, the same as the theme.
+- The rows are in the Theme door, under "Colour vision", as the groups "Line width" and "Anti-aliasing".
+
+**Why.**
+
+- A `wgpu` line is always one hardware pixel wide and has no anti-aliasing. Toolpaths were hard to see next to the 3 px egui triad (#195).
+- 2 pt and more made the dense paths into one solid area when the camera is far. Thus the default is 1.5 pt.
+- Without the lift, half of a wide line that lies on a face failed the depth test. In the pinning test, 292 px were visible on the face against 628 px for the same line in the air.
+- An instanced segment uses 32 bytes against 48 for the old vertex pair. At the overlay limit (512k segments) this is 16 MiB against 24 MiB.
+- For the fallback, a lower count never uses more memory than the user asked for.
+- `view.json` already holds the viewport's look (the origin names). `prefs.json` was already past the 400-line file limit.
+
+**Considered and dropped.**
+
+- Draw the paths with the egui painter, as the triad is drawn. This loses the depth test and is slow on large toolpaths.
+- Six full vertices for each segment (the trial). This needed approximately 135 MB at the overlay limit.
+- A per-line width class for the ground grid. The grid already fades at its rim, so it uses the one width. This can be added later with a byte in the instance colour.
+- A fallback to a higher sample count. This uses more memory than the user asked for.
+
+**Cost to change later.**
+
+- The width and the lift are uniforms and constants in `viewport/wide.rs`.
+- A new sample count is one row in `Antialias` and one check in `offered_samples`.
+- The file words are `"1"`, `"1.5"`, `"2"`, `"3"` and `"Off"`, `"2x"`, `"4x"`. A word that the build does not know reads as the default.

+The **Theme** list also sets how the viewport draws its lines.
+**Line width** (1, 1.5, 2 or 3 pt; 1.5 is the default) sets the width of
+toolpaths, height planes, outlines and axes. **Anti-aliasing** (Off, 2x
+or 4x; 4x is the default) smooths the edges of lines and models. 4x uses
+more graphics memory; turn it down on a slow integrated graphics chip.
+A count that the graphics device does not offer shows as unavailable.
+Both choices are kept for the next start.
